passage: I am Samir and I was packing my bag when I heard Tejas say to his friend Meghna, "Show me the science answers tomorrow, please. I will fail otherwise." Meghna shook her head. But instead of walking off, she said, "How about this: come to my place on Sunday at four. We go through the chapter together, and you write your own answers." Tejas looked surprised. "You would do that?" "Bring your notebook and a snack." Tejas nodded slowly, biting his lip. I do not know if he wanted to study or only wanted the answers, but he wrote SUNDAY 4 on his palm.

qa.q: What did Tejas write on his palm?
qa.a: He wrote SUNDAY 4 on his palm.

qa.q: What was Tejas worried about when he asked for the answers?
qa.a: Failing, since he said he would fail otherwise.

qa.q: What else could Meghna add if Tejas still wants only answers?
qa.a: Explain why copying will not help him in the exam itself and suggest asking the teacher for extra help, because the real problem is fear of failing.

qa.q: How might Meghna's offer have felt to Tejas?
qa.a: Surprising and a relief, since he asked "You would do that?" and nodded slowly. 🙂

grounding: A girl suggests studying together on Sunday so her friend can prepare properly instead of copying.

passage:
Thursday: Mohit caught Gopika at the water tap. "The Hindi test is on Monday. Sit next to me and let me see your answers? I'll fail otherwise." Gopika shook her head. "I won't show you answers. But you're scared of failing, right? Come to my house on Sunday. We'll do the whole chapter."
Sunday: Mohit arrived at ten with his book. Gopika's mother made poha. They read the lesson aloud, took turns asking each other the questions at the back and wrote the hard spellings three times each. By one, Mohit could answer eight of the ten without looking.
Monday: Mohit finished the test early and didn't glance sideways once. Outside he said, "I think I actually passed. On my own."

qa.q: How did Gopika feel about Mohit's request?
qa.a: She saw he was scared of failing, and felt sympathy rather than annoyance.
Offering Sunday study, because it met Mohit's real need to pass without either of them breaking the rules.

qa.q: How did Mohit feel after the test?
qa.a: Proud and relieved that he had passed on his own. 😊

grounding: Across a few days, a girl turns down a friend's request to copy and suggests studying together, meeting his real need honestly.

passage: Jaya, your friend wants your answers for the geography test? When I was in Class 6, my friend Farzana asked me the same thing. "Nazia, just let me look at your paper. If I fail again, Abbu will be so disappointed." I understood then that she wasn't lazy; she was frightened. So I said, "I can't show you in the test. But come to my house on Saturday, and we'll do the whole map together until you know it." She came. We drew the rivers on old newspaper until our fingers were blue. She passed that test, not with top marks, but with her own. After that, before every exam, we studied together on the Saturday. That's how I learned you can help a friend without breaking the rules.

qa.q: What did they draw on old newspaper?
How did Nazia understand Farzana's feelings?
qa.a: Nazia saw that Farzana was frightened, not lazy, and felt sympathy for her.

qa.q: Which choice inside the story made the difference?
qa.a: Offering Saturday study instead of showing her paper, so Farzana could pass with her own marks.

qa.q: How might Farzana have felt passing with her own marks?
qa.a: Proud and relieved, knowing the marks were really hers.

grounding: An elder recalls offering a frightened friend a study session instead of answers, meeting her need without breaking the rules.
